model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability of per-specialty medical terms when using the Mistralv0.2-Base model, both before and after fine-tuning on six distinct medical specialties: Cardio (Cardiology), Gastro (Gastroenterology), Infect (Infectious Disease), Neuro (Neurology), Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” ranges from approximately -22 to -27, with tick marks at each integer value, indicating a linear scale where lower values (more negative) reflect higher model confidence or likelihood. The horizontal axis, labeled “Per-specialty terms,” groups bars by specialty, with each group containing seven bars: one light blue bar representing the base model’s performance (labeled “Mistralv0.2-Base”) and six colored bars corresponding to the model fine-tuned on each of the six specialties (Cardio in light orange, Gastro in medium orange, Infect in dark orange, Neuro in brown-orange, Obstetrics in dark brown, and Pediatrics in very dark brown). Within each specialty group, the fine-tuned bars are consistently shorter (i.e., less negative, indicating higher probability) than the base model’s bar, suggesting improved performance after fine-tuning. The fine-tuned bars within each group are arranged left to right in the order of the legend, and the base model bar is always positioned first in each group. The chart visually demonstrates that fine-tuning on a given specialty generally yields the best performance for terms from that specialty, as the bar corresponding to the same specialty tends to be the shortest (lowest negative log probability) within its group — for example, in the “Cardio” group, the “Cardio”-fine-tuned bar is the shortest, and similarly for “Gastro,” “Infect,” etc. The chart does not include error bars or statistical annotations, and all bars are solid-colored with no shading or patterns.
